title: Unify kernel dependency graph and virtualize CUTLASS load paths for smaller runtime bundles
creator: Asha Patel
description: Reduce runtime surface-area and eliminate brittle kernel-symbol conflicts by consolidating the current ad-hoc dependency graph and introducing a virtualized CUTLASS load path. Deliver a thinner bundle artifact per runtime flavor, deterministic fallback behavior across mixed CUTLASS/CUDA versions, and a metadata-driven loader that defers heavy symbol resolution until required.
background: Over the last 18 months we added multiple patched CUTLASS builds to support model variants and quant kernels. Each variant is currently shipped in monolithic bundles which has led to large image sizes, duplicated symbols, startup contention during kernel probing, and brittle upgrade paths when host drivers or Triton change. Several production incidents (high cold-starts and rollout failures) traced back to simultaneous kernel registration and unresolved symbol collisions. This ticket centralizes the dependency graph and implements a virtualization layer to dynamically select and mount CUTLASS/quant kernels at runtime.
tasks: Inventory current kernel and CUTLASS artifacts across runtime builds (produce per-commit manifest)
Design a metadata schema for kernel capabilities, ABI tags, and fallback compatibility rules
Implement a thin virtual loader that exposes a stable symbol table and redirects requests to the selected kernel implementation
Add build changes to emit per-module thin artifacts and a consolidated dependency graph (bazel/cmake)
Integrate metadata cache with runtime startup to avoid probing N artifacts serially
Create feature flag (VIRTUAL_CUTLASS) and gated rollout in runtime CI
End-to-end tests: cross-version compatibility matrix (CUDA 12/13, Triton 2/3, CUTLASS variants)
Performance benchmarks vs current baseline (startup, per-token latency, memory overhead)
Documentation: upgrade guide, rollback steps, and playbook for incidents
Rollout: staged canary on Dedicated pools -> full rollout; monitor SLOs and error budget
acceptance_criteria: Average runtime artifact size reduced by >=20% for common model bundles compared to baseline
Median startup/kernel-probe time reduced by >=15% on p3 and a100 instances
Fallback to compatible kernel variant occurs without process restart in >=95% of tested scenarios
CI matrix (CUDA12/13 x Triton2/3 x 3 CUTLASS variants) passes on main branch
No customer-facing errors during canary rollout and metrics validate preserved output quality
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff sync with runtime, infra, and packaging teams. Agreed metadata fields and minimal schema.
2025-02-13: Prototype virtual loader that can redirect two sample CUTLASS shared objects; local benchmarks show 12% reduced probe time.
2025-02-15: Opened PR #12489 with loader and build changes. Initial CI runs failing on a flaky Triton binding test (investigating).
2025-02-18: Addressed symbol visibility by switching to explicit exported symbol table; benchmark dashboard posted (link below). Remaining: integration tests and packaging changes for thin artifacts.
tradeoffs: Indirection layer introduces a small per-call dispatch overhead (~1-2% measured) in exchange for much lower startup costs and smaller artifacts
More complex build pipeline and additional metadata to maintain; requires discipline on model onboarding to tag compatibility correctly
Initial risk around cold-path regressions — mitigated by staged canary and rollback playbook
review_feedback: Arch (Ling Zhao): prefer explicit capability Tags over fuzzy heuristics; added a new 'feature_mask' field to schema
Runtime (Eve Nguyen): ensure loader is signal-safe and avoid heap allocations during early init
Packaging (Marco Silva): require backward-compatible artifact names for existing deployment scripts
notes: Testing: add zero-downtime canary test that swaps the active CUTLASS symlink on a healthy node and validates a small prompt set
Rollout plan: canary 5% Dedicated pools for 48 hours -> 25% 72 hours -> 100% if no regressions
If a regression is detected, automatically disable VIRTUAL_CUTLASS via runtime feature flag and trigger rollback playbook
